title: AI could force 11 million US workers into new careers by 2035, says McKinsey report
source_used: International Finance (relaying McKinsey Global Institute report)
key_facts: McKinsey Global Institute: about 11 million US workers may need to change occupations by 2035.
Automation could cut labour demand by about 36 million jobs' worth of work by 2035; demand for about 41 million jobs could be created.
About 25 million of the 36 million could stay in their occupations; 11 million would need to move.
About 770,000 workers a year may need to switch occupational groups versus a long-run average of about 215,000 (roughly 3.6 times).
Customer service reps, retail sales associates, office assistants, cashiers and warehouse workers make up about a third of movers.
Strongest demand: healthcare, construction, management, professional and technical services.
AI could create 500,000 to two million jobs in new occupations; about 70% of workers could see their roles reinvented.
Range: roughly 6 million to more than 16 million movers depending on assumptions.
quote_evidence: McKinsey describes the central challenge as one of mobility rather than job scarcity.
The report does not forecast an overall collapse in US employment.
why_it_matters_hint: The issue is moving workers between jobs, not a lack of jobs.
notes: Report is from September; CBS also cites it. Re-dated as follow-up.
